meta.name: allergen_reference
meta.how_to_extend: terms and negatives are flat lists: append rows from other files (same keys). Phrases are lowercase, singular, accent-free, punctuation->space; normalize your input the same way before matching.

regulatory_status.us_fda: major allergen; the specific nut must be named
regulatory_status.eu: major allergen ('nuts'); 8 named species - pine nut is NOT on the EU list
regulatory_status.anz: mandatory; each nut named individually, generic 'tree nuts' not allowed

regulatory_status.us_fda: major allergen; since 2025 includes milk from domesticated cows, goats, sheep and other ruminants; the animal must be named
major allergen; since 2025 includes eggs of domesticated chickens, ducks, geese, quail and other fowl; species must be named
major allergen; species must be named
major allergen ('crustacean shellfish'); species must be named
NOT a major allergen (only crustacean shellfish are)

gluten_cereals.label: Cereals containing gluten (wheat is a sub-group)

regulatory_status.us_fda: wheat is a major allergen; barley, rye and oats are not
regulatory_status.eu: major allergen: wheat (such as spelt and khorasan), rye, barley, oats, or their hybridised strains
regulatory_status.canada: wheat and triticale are priority allergens; gluten sources must be declared
regulatory_status.anz: wheat, barley, oats and rye must be declared; 'gluten' declared with wheat or alone for barley/oats/rye

regulatory_status.canada: not a priority allergen (Health Canada warns peanut-allergic consumers)

sulphites.label: Sulphites (a sensitivity, not a true allergy)

regulatory_status.eu: must be declared at >10 mg/kg or 10 mg/L total SO2 (as consumed)
regulatory_status.canada: priority allergen (must be declared when part of the formulation)
